featured_reviews.name: SHARAN SUREKA
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Stand By Coffee, Worli on a Sunday after a lovely walk at the Coastal Road promenade, but the experience completely spoiled the mood. The café was in a rush hour, which we understood, but the service was extremely slow and unorganized. We ordered a green tea and a toast and sat right in front of the counter. Even after repeatedly reminding the counter boy and the chef—who were right in front of us—nothing was prepared on time. The toast came after 25 minutes, and the green tea arrived 20 minutes later, only when we got frustrated and asked them to either make it immediately or refund us. By then, the toast had already gone cold.

Another disappointing part was that while placing the order, they didn’t inform us that service charge would be added. Only after paying did we notice it on the bill. We didn’t say anything at that moment because who wants to run back for a small amount while trying to enjoy the day—but the experience that followed made it feel unfair.

When we finally gave our feedback, the staff (possibly the owner) responded casually with just a “thanks for the feedback” and showed no concern. Because of the poor service and attitude, we asked them to remove the ₹30 service charge—not for the amount, but because the service truly didn’t justify it.

I don’t recommend visiting this café on Sundays, and based on this experience, I’m unsure about other days too. This visit really ruined what could have been a great end to a beautiful walk.

The staff impressed me with how naturally they interacted with dogs — they seemed fluent in “dog talk” and genuinely lived up to the brand’s promise. It felt like a space designed not just for owners to dine, but for dogs to feel at ease, play, and socialize. Meanwhile, owners could relax, chat, network, or simply enjoy the company of fellow dog lovers, all while their pets mingled happily inside the venue.

As for the food, the pasta stood out. The pesto was flavorful, and the shrimp were generously sized — a dish that definitely left a good impression.

featured_reviews.name: SUNIKET DANGE
featured_reviews.review_text:
As Mishri’s dad and someone who genuinely loves good food, Zane’s Café has become more than just a place. It’s an experience I keep coming back to, even after 3 years.

What truly sets this place apart is the vibe. It’s not just a pet café. It’s a space thoughtfully built for pets first, and humans are lucky to be a part of it. A true leash-free environment where Mishri can just be herself, roam around freely, socialize, and feel at home. And as a pet parent, that peace of mind is priceless.

Every single detail here feels intentional, from the layout to the energy. Everything is designed to make both pets and their humans comfortable. It’s rare to find a place that gets this balance so right.

Now coming to the food, which is the other big reason I keep returning. It never disappoints. Honestly, you could close your eyes, point at anything on the menu, and you will still end up with something delicious. Every dish is consistently well made and full of flavour.

And if there’s one thing you absolutely shouldn’t miss, it’s the Zane’s X Pallonji Cold Brew. It’s something that you’ll get only here.

Great food, amazing coffee, and a space where Mishri is just as happy as I am. That’s what keeps bringing us back. 🐾

featured_reviews.name: Sachet
featured_reviews.review_text:
I rarely leave reviews, but what happened yesterday was absolutely unacceptable and I will not stay silent about it.

We bought a tub cake to celebrate a birthday. Instead, it was completely ruined when we found a fly inside the cake. A FLY. In food meant to be eaten and celebrated with.

But what makes this even more infuriating is that this was not some freak accident. When we visited the store, there were flies visibly buzzing around the very area where the cakes were on display. This is not a one-off incident.. this is a hygiene failure. The display area was clearly not maintained to any acceptable standard, and yet cakes were being sold to unsuspecting customers without a second thought.

This is a basic food safety issue. Flies are carriers of bacteria and disease.. which i ate. The fact that customers are being served food in these conditions is not just disgusting.. it is a health hazard. Had a child eaten that cake, or had this happened to someone less composed, the consequences could have been far worse.

I strongly urge the management to take immediate action not just a surface level cleanup, but a thorough review of hygiene protocols, food storage practices, and display standards. This is not acceptable for any food establishment, let alone one selling celebration cakes.

Shame on you for letting it get to this point. Do better.

Tucked away on the 3rd floor food court of Jio World Drive, Chai Chulha is a charming kiosk that serves up a steaming hot cup of comfort. This hidden gem is a must-visit for anyone craving an authentic Indian chai experience. We stopped by to try their signature Masala Chai and Grilled Bun Maska, and we were blown away!

Grilled Bun Maska

The maska (butter) is generously slathered on, adding a rich, creamy element to the dish. It's the perfect pairing with the spicy, aromatic chai.

Service

Chai Chulha in Jio World Drive is a must-visit for anyone who loves a good cup of chai. With its expertly brewed Masala Chai and delicious Grilled Bun Maska, it's a spot that will leave you feeling warm, fuzzy, and utterly satisfied.

Armani Caffè at Jio World Plaza brings a touch of Milanese sophistication to the heart of Mumbai’s luxury shopping district. It isn’t just a pitstop for shoppers; it’s a destination that mirrors the brand’s aesthetic—muted, elegant, and meticulously curated.

The Tiramisu Chicco: This is the undisputed star of the show. Shaped like a giant coffee bean, the presentation is stunning, and the flavor is nuanced—perfect for those who appreciate a dessert that isn't overly sugary.
Spaghetti ai Tre Pomodori: A masterclass in simplicity. The use of three different tomato varieties creates a depth of acidity and sweetness that sets it apart from standard pasta dishes.
Pizza & Gnocchi: The Roman-style pizzas are notably light and crispy, while the Gnocchi Alla Sorrentina is comforting and well-executed.
Coffee: Collaborating with Araku for their coffee program was a smart move. The brews are consistent, and the latte art is usually impeccable.
While it comes with the "designer price tag" you would expect at Jio World Plaza, the quality of the ingredients and the peaceful environment justify the cost. It’s an excellent choice for anyone looking for refined Italian fare in a setting that feels worlds away from the hustle of BKC. TOTALLY AVOID WASTING RS 5000.

At the onset this is probably one of the most expensive Buffets you would be having in Mumbai, priced at over 4300 plus taxes for a Dinner on a Weekday for an adult. Add to that, even as a gold accor member you probably get 20-30 percent instead of the normal 50 percent for 2 people is taxing.

The spread is decent, the variety in principal is there, but in terms of the taste and the quality of food, it’s really one of the poorest of the five stars , even considering the Leela and Lalit brands in Mumbai whose lay is very modest compared to this.

At almost 5000 you expect
1. Your veg sushi not being dumped in the refrigerator for you to pick up, questioning when it was made !

2. No juice , cold drink or mocktails are part of this offering. An advise to the team, you’re charging 5000 offering a drink probably at times could feel better than half the items on the menu.

3. I have seen just one Langarwaali daal the last 4 times I have gone here, to be honest , a Dal Makhani is the norm, if not that a top of the line dal Tadka.

4. Some dishes are borderline tasteless and on the menu just to increase the offerings on paper / website
A. Sushi - cold, refrigerated, and tasted as if it was made with zero interest.
B. Pizza Margerita- looked like an Udipi version not one served at a top 5 star, see the pictures yourself.
C. Fattoush salad, I mean if anyone has had a look at what they serve with that name, it’s embarrassing.
D. Starters like paneer tikka seem like lying there unattended for hours.
E. Many of the deserts too seem just good looking and tasting on borderline just sugar toffees.

When you come to a place , the stature of a Sofitel From the ACCOR elite stable, you expect basic standards and taste but unfortunately that’s missing.

The fact that it’s in BKC and most people have very little options for a 5 Star experience, plus because of its location the occupancy is high, is the best answer to why it’s half full during these buffets otherwise as per the taste of the food it should be  probably amongst the slowest moving places ever.

Sofitel I have over 11 million people reading this, so I’m saying this with humility please pull up and improve , make prices more competitive and the food seem like it’s made with care for the guests and hopefully the most charm would be back.

Till then all the best!!

featured_reviews.review_text:
We came here to fuel ourselves a bit before going to Enrique Iglesias, and here is my review of what this place was like

The decor was among the stronger points of the place, it has a beautiful interior with some funky looking seats as well with swings inbuilt to it.

The menu was very extensive, covering a very large number of cuisines. Normally places that say , wow, we can make all of this stuff in our kitchens, normally they're being a bit too ambitious.

We got tofu based dumplings, parmesan garlic fries, a veg sushi, the blah! special pasta, smores based pancakes and also a couple of Vietnamese coffees and a lemon based tea.

I suppose the best part of the order was dumplings, fries and the sushi, probably in that order... The tofu dumplings were delectable and perfectly well done.... The pasta was kind of average at best and the smores pancakes were ok but we've had better ones.

The Vietnamese coffees were actually among the best I've ever had and quite authentic in its preparation in that it has a VERY dense layer of thick condensed milk at the bottom and has the espresso above it. You have to mix it to get the final beverage and that's how Vietnamese coffee is supposed to be.

My friend had the tea and it could be best summarised as "tea without tea in it", which is kind of odd because tea leaves are usually a big deal in making tea, well, tea....

Service was ok but the ladies restroom had some issues which took considerable amount of time to resolve.

The price point was ok by BKC standards I suppose, but not fabulous on the value for money scale.

All in all, this place is good, but you probably may need some hit and trial to find out what their actual gastronomic speciality is.

Santacruz, listen up — **blah is turning into a pancake & matcha playground** 🥞🍵

If your love language is fluffy pancakes and your personality trait is matcha, this festival is calling your name. From **golden, cloud-soft pancakes** stacked high and dripping with indulgent toppings, to **earthy, vibrant matcha** creations that feel both comforting and cool — blah has curated a menu that hits all the right notes.

Expect pancakes that are soft, warm, and downright addictive — think classic favourites with a twist, playful flavours, and dessert plates that are meant to be shared (or not, we won’t judge). Pair that with **matcha in all its glory** — creamy lattes, refreshing blends, and dessert-style treats that balance sweetness with that signature green tea depth.

The vibe? Cozy, fun, and very Santacruz-coded. Perfect for lazy brunch dates, catch-ups with friends, or solo cafe hopping when you’re in the mood to treat yourself.

Basically, if you’re looking for a reason to step out, sip slow, and eat happy — **the Pancake & Matcha Festival at blah, Santacruz** is it. 💚🥞

featured_reviews.name: Padmini Dixit
featured_reviews.review_text:
Let’s get one thing straight: the ambience is a solid 10/10. Beautiful space, great vibe, very BKC-coded.
But unfortunately, that’s where the compliments end.

Because a restaurant’s primary purpose is food, and this place misses the mark badly.

I started with an almond soup which was the only dish I liked from what I tried. Great taste.

Next everything I tried was a highkey disappointment. The avocado tahini Caesar salad, which on the menu sounded promising: mixed lettuce, avocado slices, herbed croutons, chickpeas, tahina dressing, cherry tomatoes, parmesan shavings, and dried cranberries. What arrived was basically a bowl of lettuce with a few nuts and raisins. No avocado in sight. Had to return it. They sent a replacement, but it was pretty much the same thing, still overwhelmingly lettuce-heavy and underwhelming.

Next up, pull-me-up nachos. Another blah dish. Dry, sad, and definitely not “loaded” by any definition. Just chips, some cheese, and a few olives. That’s it.

Then came the veg bean burger, which was yet another disappointment. The fried fritters on the side were honestly pathetic, paired with stale fries that felt like they’d been sitting around way too long.

At this point, it felt like dish after dish was competing to see which one could be worse.

To end things, I tried an oat milk latte, hoping at least the coffee would save the experience, but nope. Blah and completely forgettable.

Service was okay, not bad, not memorable. But when the food keeps failing, good service can only do so much.

Honestly, I don’t know what this place is trying to be. With such a great ambience, the food quality is shockingly poor.
Pretty space, disappointing plates. Wouldn’t return unless the kitchen gets a serious reset.
